newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Novolipetsk steel hearing set for April 29.
newsitem.headline: Russian Novolipetsk steel hearing set for April 29.

text.p: A Russian court could rule in a shareholders' rights case involving steelmaker Novolipetsk Metals Combine next Tuesday, a shareholder spokesman said on Friday.

A hearing was held earlier this week at a local court in a case brought against the steel mill by U.S. investment fund Cambridge Capital Management, and the court will meet again next week to consider further evidence, the spokesman said.
But he said the Lipetsk court was waiting to receive further evidence requested in other cases involving the same company.
"There may be a decision on Tuesday on Cambridge Capital Management," the spokesman said.
Cambridge chairman Thomas Gaffney said in a statement released after the hearing this week he was optimistic about the outcome of the case.
"(The) proceedings went well and we are optimistic about winning," Gaffney said.

Cambridge, which owns 17.2 percent of the plant, and, in a separate case, Renaissance Capital's Sputnik Fund, which owns nine percent, say management refused to consider candidates to the board of directors.
"It's a shame that the defendants have focused so much of their time, talent and energy to keep us out using any excuses available no matter how absurd," Gaffney said.
"It's too bad, because CCM's goal is to increase the profitability and value of the plant."
Senior Novolipetsk managers could not be reached for comment on Friday, but have said they acted in accordance with company rules.

Another shareholder, Bank MFK, associated with powerful Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian), and owner of 15 percent of Novolipetsky Metallurgichesky Kombinat (NLMK), says it was stripped of its voting rights last year.

But the spokesman, who did not wish to be named, said whatever the court decided in regard to Cambridge's claims would have little bearing on the outcome of the cases brought by their fellow shareholders.
"(A decision) would be interesting, but since Russia doesn't operate on precedent, you would be wrong to draw conclusions on the outcome of the others."
The spokesman said Bank MFK, whose case is being filed on its behalf by the State Property Fund and the Sputnik Fund expected their hearings to be scheduled soon.
